step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates an automated ChatOps deployment pipeline integrating AWS CodePipeline with Slack for interactive approval steps. First, during the manual approval stage, CodePipeline triggers an SNS notification (Flow 0, seq 0). SNS invokes a notification Lambda function (Flow 0, seq 1), which uses webhooks to post an interactive Yes/No approval box into a designated Slack channel (Flow 0, seq 2). When an authorized team member interacts with the button in Slack, an HTTP request is made to API Gateway (Flow 1, seq 0). API Gateway triggers an approval Lambda function (Flow 1, seq 1), which calls back into CodePipeline to approve and resume the deployment process to Production (Flow 1, seq 2).

graph.name: OpenFit ChatOps Continuous Deployment Pipeline

nodes.name: Lambda (Notification)

nodes.name: Slack
nodes.notes: Displays interactive Yes/No message box for deployment approval.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Exposes REST API endpoint triggered by user interactions in Slack.

nodes.name: Lambda (Approval)

edges.notes: CodePipeline approval step sends notification event to SNS.
SNS topic invokes the notification Lambda function.
Notification Lambda sends webhook message creating a Yes/No box in Slack.
Button action in Slack triggers API Gateway endpoint.
API Gateway invokes approval Lambda function.
Approval Lambda signals CodePipeline to proceed with production deployment.
